title: Central torus and unipotent quotient of a smooth connected nilpotent group
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], and fix an algebraic closure $\bar k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups below are affine $k$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness mean [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group which becomes $\mathbf G_m^r$ over $\bar k$, for some integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. Unipotent means admitting, for some $n\geq1$, a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion] into the upper unitriangular group $\mathcal U_{n,k}\subseteq\operatorname{GL}_{n,k}$ [def-sc-general-linear-group]: its $A$-points are upper triangular matrices with all diagonal entries $1$, for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$. Let $G$ be smooth, connected and nilpotent, where nilpotent means that there is a finite descending series of closed normal subgroup schemes $G=G_0\supseteq G_1\supseteq\cdots\supseteq G_s=1$ such that commutators of $G$ with $G_i$ land in $G_{i+1}$ after every commutative algebra extension. There exist a central torus $T\subseteq G$, a smooth connected unipotent affine group $Q$, and a faithfully flat homomorphism $q:G\to Q$ whose scheme-theoretic kernel is $T$ and which represents the fppf quotient $G/T$. Here the quotient is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/T(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings. If $T=1$, then $q$ is an isomorphism. No perfectness assumption on $k$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 16.47(a),(c), printed p.341, as used in the first case of the proof of Proposition 17.81, p.379; Theorem 14.5(a),(b), pp.281–282. Quotient by the central smooth torus is the represented fppf quotient (Proposition 5.25, Corollary 5.26, Theorem 5.28 and Proposition 5.29, p.105).

proof.text: Take the closed commutative centre $Z=Z(G)$ from [lem-sfb-affine-group-centre-base-change]. Apply [lem-sfb-commutative-multiplicative-part] to $C=Z$, and put $T=Z_s$. Thus $T$ is of multiplicative type and central, hence normal in $G$. By [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry], form $q:G\to Q=G/T$, an affine finite-type represented fppf quotient with kernel $T$, faithfully flat and finitely presented.

source.place: Theorems 16.13(a), p.328, and 16.47(a), p.341; Propositions 5.25–5.29, p.105.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-nilpotent-quotient-unipotent-centre] to $G$, $D=T$, and this quotient: $G$ is connected and nilpotent by hypothesis, and $T$ contains every multiplicative-type subgroup of $Z(G)$ by its construction. It gives that $Q$ is connected and nilpotent and $Z(Q)$ is unipotent. Therefore [lem-sfb-nilpotent-unipotent-centre] gives a closed immersion $Q\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{m,k}$ for some $m\geq1$. The smoothness clause of [lem-sfb-affine-normal-quotient-geometry] makes $Q$ smooth because $G$ is smooth.

source.place: Lemmas 16.45–16.46 and Theorem 16.47(a), pp.340–341; Corollary 5.26, p.105.

proof.text: Put $F=\bar k$. Smooth base change [lem-pc-proper-base-change](2) makes $G_F$ smooth. Its identity is a $k$-rational point, so [lem-sbc-connected-rational-point-geometrically-connected] makes $G_F$ connected. The base-changed central series is still central on every $F$-algebra. Each factor is commutative since $[G_i,G_i]\subseteq[G,G_i]\subseteq G_{i+1}$, so $G_F$ is solvable. Lie–Kolchin [lem-sfb-lie-kolchin-triangular-embedding] gives a closed immersion $G_F\hookrightarrow B_n$. Apply [lem-sfb-triangular-diagonal-kernel]: its diagonal quotient $d:G_F\to D$ has kernel $V\subseteq U_n$, a group section $s:D\to G_F$, and $D$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup of $\mathbf G_m^n$.

source.place: Theorem 16.47(c), p.341; Theorem 16.30, pp.334–335; Theorem 16.26(a) and Corollary 16.33, pp.332–336.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-split-torus-subgroups-diagonalizable], write $D\simeq D_F(M)$. The closed immersion of $Q$ into $\mathcal U_m$ from step 2 remains a closed immersion over $F$: on coordinate rings, a surjection stays surjective after tensoring with $F$. Hence [lem-sfb-diagonalizable-to-unipotent-trivial] applied to $q_Fs:D\to Q_F$ gives $q_Fs=1$. Its image therefore lies in $\ker q_F=T_F$ (kernels commute with base change by the defining fibre-product equation). Thus $s$ factors as $j:D\to T_F$ and $(d|_{T_F})j=1_D$.

source.place: Corollary 14.18(b), p.284, in the triangular realization used for Theorem 16.47(c).

proof.text: The kernel $I$ of $d|_{T_F}$ is the closed intersection $T_F\cap V$. Since $V\subseteq U_n$, also $I\subseteq U_n$, so $I$ is unipotent directly from its closed immersion. The target $T_F$ is of multiplicative type by step 1. Apply [lem-sfb-unipotent-to-multiplicative-trivial] to the inclusion $I\to T_F$: it is trivial. As that inclusion is injective on every algebra, $I(A)=\{1\}$ for every $F$-algebra $A$. For $t\in T_F(A)$ the element $t\,j(d(t))^{-1}$ lies in $I(A)$; hence $t=j(d(t))$. These equalities are natural in $A$ and prove that $j$ and $d|_{T_F}$ are inverse group-scheme morphisms.

source.place: Corollaries 14.17–14.18, p.284; explicit complementary-factor calculation underlying Lemma 16.44, p.340.

proof.text: Thus $T_F\simeq D$. The group $D$ is smooth, connected and a closed subgroup of a split torus, so [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus] makes it a torus. Over the algebraically closed field $F$, its torus definition says $D\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$ for some $r\geq0$. Therefore $T_F\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$, which is precisely the torus condition on $T$ over $k$. Together with steps 1–2 this proves the asserted central torus and smooth connected unipotent fppf quotient, without perfectness of $k$.

If $T=1$, the presheaf $A\mapsto G(A)/T(A)$ is exactly $A\mapsto G(A)$. Since $q$ represents its fppf sheafification and the represented group functor is already an fppf sheaf, its sheafification map is an isomorphism. Thus $q$ is an isomorphism of represented functors, hence of group schemes.

source.place: Definition 5.20, p.104; Section 5(j), pp.116–118; the defining universal property of the represented quotient.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 16.47(a),(c), pp.340–341. The smoothness argument is written through the triangular quotient after algebraic closure, using the same Lie–Kolchin input and complementary-factor calculation as 16.47(c) and 16.44.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q128-4f56ff7d9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Milne, Algebraic Groups: 16.13(a),(b) and Note 16.17 (p.328–329), and 16.43–16.48 (pp.340–341). The item is 16.47(a)+(c) for smooth G. Its statement is unchanged, and this is a first split, not a 2026-10-21 re-split. Step 1: T=Z(G)_s, using the centre node and new node 16.13(a), and the quotient node gives q with kernel T. Step 2: new node 16.45, then new node 16.46, make Q unipotent; the quotient node's smoothness clause makes Q smooth. Step 3: over k̄, G is smooth and connected (tool uses: smooth base change, identity rational point). Nilpotent implies solvable, written out against the Lie–Kolchin node's definition. Lie–Kolchin plus the triangular diagonal-kernel node give V, D and the section s. Step 4: D is diagonalizable, Q_F embeds in U_m, so q_F∘s=1 and s factors through T_F. Step 5: T_F∩V is unipotent and multiplicative, hence trivial, and the t·j(d(t))^{-1} computation gives T_F≅D. Step 6: D is a smooth connected subgroup of a split torus, so it is a torus, hence T is a torus. Step 7: elementary. I checked every hypothesis. The new nodes are 16.13(a) with field extension, 16.45 and 16.46. All three are true over any field without smoothness, and I tested them on G_m, G_a, μ_p, α_p, μ_p×α_p and U_n. None restates the item or one of its clauses. A DAG-wide and blueprint search found no duplicate; the commutative product node covers only algebraically closed fields, and the subtorus node is a different statement. There is no cycle. I accept the two generic tool_uses (precedent: central-extension-of-tori). Batch-5: all five flagged citations are algebraic-group lemmas. Their closure reaches trf only through generic descent and flatness nodes (scheme-cover descent datum, fppf covering base change, flat tensor injection, smooth fpqc descent). These are not trace-formula or Poincaré-duality steps, so I accept them. Cosmetic: the new nodes' inherited from.place gives p.110 for Thm 5.28 while the item source says p.105. No changes.
